title: Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Island - The Historic Jewel of Andaman Islands
content:
Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Island - The Historic Jewel of Andaman Islands

Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Island, formerly known as Ross Island, is one of the most fascinating destinations in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Located just a short ferry ride from Port Blair, the island offers a unique combination of history, natural beauty, and colonial heritage.

Once the administrative headquarters of the British in the Andaman Islands, the island today stands as a living museum where nature has reclaimed old colonial structures. Visitors can explore historic ruins, scenic viewpoints, lush greenery, and learn about the island's significant role in India's freedom movement.

The island is among the most popular tourist attractions near Port Blair and is often included in Andaman sightseeing itineraries.

History of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Island

The island gained prominence after the British established their administrative headquarters here in the mid-19th century. It became the center of British administration in the Andaman Islands and was often referred to as the "Paris of the East."

The British developed impressive infrastructure on the island, including:

  • Government offices
  • Residences
  • Churches
  • Hospitals
  • Bakeries
  • Water treatment plants
  • Tennis courts
  • Swimming pools

The island served as the headquarters for British officials overseeing the nearby Cellular Jail and penal settlements.

During World War II, the Japanese occupied the island from 1942 to 1945. In December 1943, Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose visited the Andaman Islands and ceremonially hoisted the Indian national flag, marking a historic moment in India's struggle for independence.

To honor his contribution, Ross Island was officially renamed Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Island in 2018.

Why Visit Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Island?

The island offers a rare opportunity to witness:

  • British colonial architecture
  • Historical ruins covered by tree roots
  • Stunning sea views
  • Rich biodiversity
  • Historical significance
  • Photography opportunities
  • Peaceful walking trails

It is one of the few places in India where history and nature coexist so beautifully.

Major Attractions on the Island

1. British Colonial Ruins

The island's biggest attraction is its collection of colonial-era structures.

Visitors can explore remains of:

  • Chief Commissioner's Residence
  • Government buildings
  • Church
  • Bakery
  • Printing press
  • Officers' quarters

Many of these buildings are now intertwined with giant roots and tropical vegetation, creating a unique and picturesque landscape.

2. Chief Commissioner's House

This was once the grand residence of the British administrative head of the Andaman Islands.

Although partially in ruins today, it remains one of the most photographed landmarks on the island.

3. Historic Church

The remains of the old church reflect the island's colonial past and showcase British architectural influences.

4. Japanese Bunkers

Constructed during World War II, these bunkers provide insight into the island's strategic importance during the Japanese occupation.

5. Light and Sound Show

An engaging Light and Sound Show narrates the history of the island, from British settlement to Japanese occupation and India's freedom movement.

The show offers visitors a deeper understanding of the island's heritage.

6. Wildlife Encounters

The island is home to:

  • Deer
  • Peacocks
  • Rabbits
  • Various bird species

These animals roam freely and add to the island's charm.

Natural Beauty of the Island

The island is surrounded by crystal-clear waters and lush tropical vegetation.

Visitors can enjoy:

  • Scenic walking trails
  • Panoramic viewpoints
  • Ocean photography
  • Nature exploration

The combination of history and natural beauty makes the island one of the most photogenic locations in Andaman.

Best Time to Visit

  • October to February: The most pleasant season with cool temperatures and ideal sightseeing conditions.
  • March to May: Good weather for exploration and photography.
  • June to September: Monsoon season may affect ferry schedules and outdoor activities.

How to Reach Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Island

  • By Air: The nearest airport is Veer Savarkar International Airport in Port Blair.
  • By Ferry: Regular ferries operate from Port Blair's Water Sports Complex to the island. The journey takes approximately 15-20 minutes. Visitors usually combine the island visit with North Bay Island excursions.

Entry Fee and Timings

The island is generally open during daytime hours.

Visitors may need:

  • Ferry tickets
  • Entry tickets
  • Charges for Light and Sound Show (if applicable)

It is advisable to check current rates before travel.

Travel Tips

  • Carry drinking water.
  • Wear comfortable walking shoes.
  • Carry sunscreen and a hat.
  • Start early to avoid crowds.
  • Keep your camera ready for wildlife and historic ruins.
  • Follow environmental guidelines and avoid littering.

Nearby Attractions

Many travelers combine their visit with:

  • Cellular Jail
  • Corbyn’s Cove Beach
  • North Bay Island
  • Chidiya Tapu
  • Anthropological Museum

Once the administrative headquarters of the British, the island is now famous for its fascinating ruins, Japanese bunkers, and lush tropical landscapes. A visit offers a perfect blend of history, heritage, and natural beauty, making it one of the top attractions in Andaman.

faqs.question: Why was Ross Island renamed?
faqs.answer: Ross Island was renamed Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Island in honor of Netaji's historic visit in 1943.

faqs.question: How far is the island from Port Blair?
faqs.answer: The island is located approximately 2 kilometers from Port Blair and can be reached by ferry.

faqs.question: How much time is needed to explore the island?
faqs.answer: Most visitors spend 2-3 hours exploring the island.

faqs.question: Is the island suitable for families?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is a family-friendly destination with historical and natural attractions.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit?
faqs.answer: October to May is considered the best period for visiting.
